annotations.title: Get All Standards for a Grade

description:
Return every standard for one subject and grade in a single call, as a nested tree: the one-call alternative to repeated browse_standards calls (e.g. 'list all the 4th grade ELA standards'). `subject` and `grade` are required. Each node has `id`, `code`, `title`, `cf_item_type`, `kind`, `strand_code`, `gmas` / `ald` coverage flags, and nested `children`. It carries no achievement-level or test text; follow up on specific codes with get_standard_details or lookup_standards_by_code. Retired rows and empty containers are left out.

High school (grades 9-12) is organized by course, with up to 18 courses per grade. Without `course`, a high-school grade returns `courses` (each course's `id`, `code`, `title`, and `standard_count`) instead of the full tree; call again with `course` set to a title, code, or id from that list (or a name like 'algebra i') for that course's standards. `strand_code` narrows any tree to one strand. Returns `tree`, `node_count`, and `standard_count` (nodes that carry a code).

course.description: High-school course: a title, code, or id from the `courses` list, or a name like 'algebra i' or 'biology'.
course.title: Course

grade.description: One grade: 'K' (or 'KG') or '01' through '12'. '1' through '9' also work.
grade.title: Grade

strand_code.description: Optional strand, by code ('NR') or name ('Numerical Reasoning'). describe_vocabulary lists the strands for each subject.
strand_code.title: Strand Code
